title: habitat component contract
description: The YAML front matter of a components/<name>.md file. Each field exists because an agent needs it to use the component without guessing. Any string value may start with 'TODO' while the file is a draft; the validator counts them, and a file marked 'reviewed' must have none.

status.description: 'draft' while the AI and designer are still filling it in. 'reviewed' once a person has checked every field; a reviewed file may not contain TODOs. 'deprecated' when the component is being retired: agents must not use it, and should use replacedBy instead.

replacedBy.description: For a deprecated component, the canonical name of the component to use instead. Must exist in components/.

owner.description: Who answers questions about this component and approves changes to it: a person or a team.

lastReviewed.description: When a person last checked this file against Figma and code (YYYY-MM-DD). Stale documentation is worse than none, because an agent follows it with confidence; the validator warns after six months.

figma.description: Where this component lives in Figma, so the agent (and the next person) can go back to the source.

name.description: Canonical name plus any aliases, so the same component is referred to consistently. Maps to agent-ready: naming consistency.

aliases.description: Other names this has been called, to be normalised to the canonical name.

purpose.description: Why this component exists and what job it does, described by purpose not appearance. 'Lets a user commit to an action' not 'a rounded rectangle with a label'. Maps to agent-ready: description coverage and quality.

props.description: Every prop the agent can set. Usually lifted from the Figma component properties. Maps to agent-ready: component properties.

figma.description: The matching Figma component property, so an agent can translate between the canvas and code.

property.description: The property name as it appears in Figma, e.g. 'Type' or 'Show icon'.

values.description: Prop value to Figma value, when they differ, e.g. { primary: 'Primary' }.

anatomy.description: The component's parts and layout, read from its Figma layers and auto layout. Without this, an agent knows which tokens a component uses but not how it is put together, which is where generated UI visibly drifts.

required.description: Whether the part is always present.

visibleWhen.description: The condition that shows an optional part, e.g. 'loading is true'.

layout.description: Auto layout, with spacing given as token names.

padding.description: Token names, CSS order, e.g. 'space.md space.lg'.

width.description: 'hug', 'fill', or a token or constraint, e.g. 'fill, max 480px'.

variants.description: Named variants and, crucially, WHEN to use each. Maps to agent-ready: component coverage and description quality.

whenToUse.description: The decision rule the agent should apply to pick this variant.

evidence.description: Ids of the research insights behind this decision, e.g. ['INS-004'].

states.description: The interaction and status states the component defines. An agent that cannot see a state will not build it. Maps to agent-ready: state completeness.

name.description: e.g. default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading.

tokens.description: Which design token is bound to which visual property. Binding, not mere existence, is what an agent can act on. Maps to agent-ready: token binding.

relationships.description: Where this component lives and what it works with, so the agent places it correctly. Maps to agent-ready: relationships and hierarchy.

antiPatterns.description: Explicit refusals: what the agent must never do with this component. This is the judgement the agent cannot infer on its own, and the part Figma cannot hold, so it comes from interviewing the designer. Maps to agent-ready: the refusals that keep generated UI honest.

never.description: The forbidden action, e.g. 'place two primary buttons in the same view'.

because.description: The reason, so the rule survives paraphrase.

source.description: Who stated this rule and when, e.g. 'Sam (design lead), 2026-09-20', so the reason can be traced back to a decision.

evidence.description: Ids of the research insights this rule rests on, e.g. ['INS-004'], so the reason can be traced to what users actually did.

accessibility.description: How the component behaves for assistive technology and keyboards. Maps to agent-ready: accessibility annotations.

keyboard.description: Key interactions, e.g. 'Enter and Space activate'.

focus.description: Focus behaviour and visible focus treatment.

content.description: Real example content, never lorem ipsum, so the agent sees how the component is actually used. Maps to agent-ready: real content.

codeConnect.description: Optional. The bridge from this contract to a real implementation in code, and the mapping between Figma props and code props. Maps to agent-ready: the Code Connect bridge.

implementation.description: Path or import for the component source, e.g. './Button.tsx' or '@acme/ui/Button'.

propMap.description: Figma prop name to code prop name.
